synopsis: 42 tests executed across five suites. One helper-reach test failed because the expected blocked-helper event was absent; all other selected tests passed. The failed case uses the default fire decision before later hallway smoke, which can now evacuate occupants before the blocked-helper condition arises.

failures.diagnosis: The test requires an assistance-blocked event for the child after the hallway-smoke variant, but no matching event exists. Source currently selects the default early-escape behavior rather than explicitly leaving people inside until smoke blocks reachability.
failures.fix: Freeze initial snapshot and external schedule; provide an explicit supported delay/remaining-inside intervention for the blocked-helper branch so the late condition is actually exercised. Keep the expected critical helper-reach evidence, exact cause link, no unsafe route and no re-entry recommendation assertions. Add a complementary timely-exit branch asserting no later blocked-helper penalty after successful evacuation.

recommendations: Check actual committed occupant state at the hallway event before deciding whether event absence is a product bug. Do not reintroduce a blocked-helper warning for already evacuated people merely to satisfy the older test.
Rerun the same selected set after making the causal setup explicit. Preserve no-route and smoke exclusion coverage.
limitations: Diagnosis is source-supported likely test-setup drift; no inspected state trace explicitly prints occupant location at the late event. Verify the controlled branch with deterministic receipt.
No provider or native behavior verified by this run.
